title: Rolling Policy Conductor for Safe Auto-Apply of Optimize Recommendations
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Build a 'Policy Conductor' service that orchestrates safe, reversible application of Optimize-generated batching and KV-caching configs across customer workloads. The conductor should centralize gating logic, canary splits, progressive traffic shifts, and human-in-the-loop approval hooks so that model-driven cost savings can be applied with low blast radius and clear observability.

Scope:
- Accept Optimize suggestions (batching and cache profile changes) from the optimizer pipeline and represent them as versioned proposals.
- Support configurable rollout policies: percentage-based canary, time-based ramp, metric-based gating (latency, token cost delta, error-rate), and tenant whitelists/blacklists.
- Provide an approvals workflow (auto-approve rules for low-risk changes + manual approval UI for high-risk changes).
- Automatic rollback logic when canary metrics regress beyond thresholds; provide one-click revert and staged rollback strategies.
- Emit explainable audit records for every change (who/what triggered, policy used, metrics observed).
- Integrate with Console for per-route dashboards and with Alerts for threshold breaches.

High-level design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Centralized conductor service vs. decentralized per-cluster controller: we will start centralized for consistency and easier auditability; evaluate moving a lightweight controller to Dedicated nodes if scale/latency requires.
- Metric selection: prioritize 95th-latency, mean-cost-per-token, and failure-rate. These cover user experience, economic impact, and correctness.
- Safety-first defaults: require manual approval for changes that increase batching beyond preset limits or change KV cache eviction policies. Auto-approve simple prefix-cache TTL/size reductions under safe thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy Conductor can accept and store proposals, with versioning and checksum.
- Rollouts can be executed with percentage canary (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) and automated ramps.
- Canary gate: automatic pause and rollback when 95th-latency increases > 15% for 5m or error-rate increases > 0.5pp.
- Manual approval path: PM/Eng/Customer Ops can approve/reject from Console; timestamped audit log recorded.
- A/B attribution: produce per-candidate telemetry showing token-cost delta and response-quality change (using existing eval harness).
- One-click rollback that restores prior runtime config with minimal downtime and records reason.

Implementation notes:
- New DB table: policy_proposals (id, proposal_blob_checksum, status_string, created_by, approvers_csv, created_at, updated_at). Use existing Postgres cluster and follow migration guidelines.
- API primitives: POST /proposals, GET /proposals/{id}, POST /proposals/{id}/rollout (body: policy), POST /proposals/{id}/approve, POST /proposals/{id}/rollback. Keep REST surface small; SDK wrappers will be built later.
- Controller behavior: periodic reconciliation loop to advance rollout steps; reconcile idempotently and emit fine-grained events to event-bus (Kafka).
- Telemetry: wire per-step metrics to Console: canary_traffic_pct, canary_latency_p95, canary_error_rate, cost_delta_tokens, rollback_count. Create dashboards and alerts.
- Testing: unit tests for policy rules, integration tests using traffic replay harness, and a staged canary in staging with synthetic traffic.

Open questions:
- Do we require SLO-based gating to be configurable per-customer? (Recommendation: yes, default to org-level SLOs but allow overrides for Dedicated/private.)
- How will the conductor authenticate operations coming from optimizer service vs. operator-initiated changes? (Use mTLS + service principals; require approver identity in audit logs.)

Risk assessment and mitigation:
- Risk: aggressive batching could raise p95 latency. Mitigation: conservative defaults + early canary on small % of traffic + automatic rollback.
- Risk: state drift between conductor and runtime. Mitigation: reconciliation loop + periodic checksum verification + fallback mode that prefers runtime safe defaults.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement proposal ingestion + storage + basic UI in Console (backend + provisional Console endpoints) in staging.
2) Small internal canary on 2 non-critical tenants for 2 weeks.
3) Expand to internal production traffic with telemetry-backed guardrails.
4) Open beta for select customers with opt-in flag.
5) GA when metrics show stable cost improvements and no service regressions across canaries.

Operational runbook excerpt:
- If canary triggers rollback: notify #optimize-ops, mute further auto-apply for 24h for that org, create incident with severity determined by customer_impact.
- For failed rollback: manual intervention required by infra on-call; revert DB state and re-deploy prior config.

Notes for security/compliance:
- All proposal approvals must be logged to the audit trail and integrated with KMS for any secrets involved.
- Security review required before exposing manual-approval endpoints to customer-managed Private deployments.
